newsitem.title: FRANCE: France protests over Spanish truckers' strike.
newsitem.headline: France protests over Spanish truckers' strike.

text.p: France has protested to Madrid over a road blockade by striking Spanish truck drivers, asking it to ensure protection of stranded French truckers, the French Foreign Ministry said on Thursday.
French police barred trucks from driving into northwest Spain.
The Foreign Ministry said France's envoy to Madrid called on Spanish junior foreign minister Ramon de Miguel on Wednesday to voice concern over the worsening situation of stranded drivers.
The Spanish Interior Ministry was requested to ensure their protection and avoid a repeat of violent incidents at roadblocks in the Santander region.
The ministry did not spell out what occurred. But French truckers told radio stations they were stopped at knifepoint.
A French truck ran over and killed a Spanish striker who tried to stop it early on Thursday.

They said trucks would not be allowed to enter Spain through the Basque region and urged road haulage companies to put off deliveries to northwestern Spain -- from the Atlantic Ocean to Castilla-Leon.
Trucks were still allowed to drive into northeast Spain.
More than 100 trucks are waiting on the French side of the border, their drivers fearful of becoming stranded in Spain.
Tension has been mounting in Spain where a week-long truckers' strike has spread to almost all of the north of the country.
The blockade was an ironic repeat of last year's 12-day strike by French truckers which disrupted much of Western Europe and left hundreds of foreign truck drivers stranded, including many Spaniards.
Spanish truckers are pushing for a restructuring of their sector, retirement at 60 instead of 65, and renegotiation of gasoline costs.
French truck drivers won a number of concessions last year, including wage rises and retirement at 55 instead of 60.
